items.q: Combine the fractions in the numerator to evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 3} \frac{\frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{3}}{x - 3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 - x = -(x - 3)</annotation></semantics></math>, so the result is negative: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The common denominator is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3x</annotation></semantics></math>, which heads to 9, not 3.

items.q: What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 5} \frac{x^2 - 25}{x^2 - 10x + 25}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: It does not exist: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x + 5}{x - 5}</annotation></semantics></math> is unbounded near 5.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, because the top and bottom both become 0 when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 5</annotation></semantics></math>.
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>, because the top becomes 0.
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{10}{0}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 3} \frac{|x - 3|}{x - 3}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: It does not exist: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> from the left, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> from the right.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, because near <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3</annotation></semantics></math> the top and bottom have equal sizes, so they cancel.
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>, because the top becomes 0.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x - 3</annotation></semantics></math> is negative.

items.q: Rationalize the denominator to evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 4} \frac{x - 4}{\sqrt{x} - 2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Here the square root is on the bottom: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>→</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(x - 4)(\sqrt{x} + 2)}{x - 4} = \sqrt{x} + 2 \to 4</annotation></semantics></math>, not its reciprocal.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x} + 2</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 + 2 = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 1} \frac{2x^2 - x - 1}{x - 1}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>
It does not exist.

items.q: Substituting <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3</annotation></semantics></math> into which function gives a nonzero number divided by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 3} f(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That comes from factoring the numerator as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x + 2)(x - 3)</annotation></semantics></math>, which multiplies out to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 - x - 6</annotation></semantics></math>. The right factors are <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 2)(x - 3)</annotation></semantics></math>.

Substituting gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>0</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{0}{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is not the value 0. It says to rewrite: cancel the common factor <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x - 3</annotation></semantics></math> and substitute again.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></munder><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 3} g(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: After multiplying by the conjugate, the denominator is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x + 1} + 2</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 + 2 = 4</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, not 2.

That is the reciprocal. The simplified expression is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\sqrt{x + 1} + 2}</annotation></semantics></math>, so the limit is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: What can you conclude about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></munder><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 3} h(x)</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: It equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math>, the value of the numerator at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3</annotation></semantics></math>

It does not exist; <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is unbounded near <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3</annotation></semantics></math>

It equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, after the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x - 3</annotation></semantics></math> terms cancel
It can be found by factoring and cancelling first

items.q: Which functions must be rewritten (factored, rationalized or simplified) before their limit at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3</annotation></semantics></math> can be found by substitution?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 1^-} p(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, the formula for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ge 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Approaching from the left, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x < 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so use the first piece.

Substituting into the first piece gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>0</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{0}{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, not 0. Factor: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(x + 3)(x - 1)}{x - 1} = x + 3</annotation></semantics></math>, which is 4 at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 1^+} p(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is the left-hand limit. From the right, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x) = x^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, which approaches 2.

items.q: Which statement about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munder><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 1} p(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is true?
options: It equals 2, because the value of the function <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(1)</annotation></semantics></math> is 2
It equals 3, the average of the two one-sided limits
It does not exist: the one-sided limits are 4 and 2
It equals 4, the limit of the factored left-hand piece

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></munder><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -2} p(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Near <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -2</annotation></semantics></math> the input is less than 1, so the first piece applies: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4 - 4 - 3}{-3} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

Check the signs: the numerator is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2)^2 + 2(-2) - 3 = -3</annotation></semantics></math> and the denominator is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2 - 1 = -3</annotation></semantics></math>, so the quotient is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The expression <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^2 - 16}{x - 4}</annotation></semantics></math> equals a simpler expression at every <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 4</annotation></semantics></math>. Write that simpler expression (no fraction bar).

mistakes.why: Factor the difference of squares: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 - 16 = (x - 4)(x + 4)</annotation></semantics></math>. Cancelling <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x - 4</annotation></semantics></math> leaves <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

You cannot cancel a term from part of the numerator. Factor first: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 4)(x + 4)</annotation></semantics></math>, then cancel the whole factor <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x - 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\frac{1}{x + 2} - \frac{1}{2}}{x}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Watch the sign: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x + 2} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2 - (x + 2)}{2(x + 2)} = \frac{-x}{2(x + 2)}</annotation></semantics></math>.
